title: Responses API compatibility conformance playbook and runtime bridge
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create a pragmatic conformance playbook and a lightweight runtime bridge to map Redwood's internal Responses surface to the OpenAI Responses API semantics. The goal is not to be a lossy 1:1 polyfill, but to provide deterministic behavior, clear lossiness signals, and safe fallbacks for customers migrating integrations that expect OpenAI Responses features (streaming chunks, tool/function call handoff, and structured output schemas). Deliverables: (1) a conformance checklist and lossiness taxonomy, (2) a small runtime translation layer (bridge) that can be enabled per-tenant or per-route, (3) an automated test harness that runs canonical OpenAI contract tests and reports deltas, and (4) rollout/runbook for progressive exposure with telemetry and guardrails.
background: Multiple customers and internal personas are attempting to migrate from OpenAI's Responses API. We've observed subtle behavior differences in streaming chunk boundaries, tool call signals, structured output enforcement, and error semantics. Existing compatibility tickets are fragmented; teams have built ad-hoc adapters. This ticket consolidates a production-ready playbook with a short-lived bridge that reduces migration risk while we continue improving native runtime semantics.
acceptance_criteria: A conformance checklist covering 18 compatibility points (streaming framing, role/metadata preservation, function/tool signal header parity, structured JSON schema enforcement, edge case error codes) exists and is reviewed by runtime+SDK+QA
Bridge implementation that translates Requests/Responses to OpenAI-like events with opt-in per-route config and <50ms added median latency on p50 for controlled test load
Automated test harness that runs 100 canonical scenarios (including streaming+toolcall interleavings) and emits a delta report with lossiness classifications
Telemetry events and dashboard widgets showing compatibility mode usage, regression counts, and customer-facing loss alerts
Rollout plan (canary, staged ramp, automated rollback) documented with playbook steps and communication templates
tasks: Draft conformance checklist and lossiness taxonomy – initial pass by Feb 18
Design runtime bridge API surface and wiring (per-tenant flag and per-route override)
Implement event translator for streaming frames and function-call handoff
Extend response serializer to optionally inject OpenAI-compatible metadata and chunk markers
Build test harness that replays canonical OpenAI response sequences and captures diffs
Create telemetry schema and Grafana dashboard for compatibility regressions
Run internal canary with two sandbox customers and gather feedback
Prepare customer migration notes and SDK snippets for common languages
progress_updates: 2025-02-15: Kickoff meeting with runtime, SDK and QA. Agreed scope: shipping a bridge that is explicitly opt-in and transient. Action: Aisha to draft checklist; Mateo to prototype streaming translator.

2025-02-20: Checklist v0.1 completed (18 points). Early findings: OpenAI streams often split tokens mid-sentence; our runtime batches tokens which changes chunk boundaries. Need a chunk-alignment mode for compatibility.

2025-02-25: Prototype translator implemented for streaming events. P50 latency impact measured at +32ms under toy load. Initial toolcall handoff preserves function name but differed on 'finished' sentinel — added sentinel mapping rule.
2025-03-01: Test harness scaffolding completed. Running first 50 canonical scenarios; 12 showed structural mismatches with our serializer when structured JSON contains escaped newlines.
2025-03-04: Telemetry events defined and patched into bridge path. Dashboard layout drafted; started wiring synthetic tests to populate graphs. Preparing canary invite for two sandbox tenants.
decisions: Bridge will be opt-in via per-tenant feature flag and per-route override to avoid surprising behavior for existing customers
We will signal lossiness explicitly in both response headers and compliance telemetry rather than attempting silent remediation
Bridge implementation language: Go (integrates with runtime hot path) with a thin JS shim in SDKs for client-side behaviors
Do not attempt to emulate every OpenAI API quirk; prioritize determinism and observability and document unsupported behaviors in migration notes
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Bridge increases surface area and latency. Mitigation: Opt-in only, p99 latency SLAs in stress tests, and automated rollback if latency regressions detected
Risk: Silent behavioral differences cause customer regressions. Mitigation: Explicit lossiness headers and pre-migration diff reports for each customer’s sample prompts
Risk: False-positives in delta detection. Mitigation: Fuzzy match thresholds in test harness and manual review workflow for ambiguous cases
qa_plan: Create 100 canonical scenarios covering streaming boundaries, toolcall handoffs, structured-output validation, and error induction
Run harness against the bridge and against a native runtime baseline; generate delta report with lossiness class per scenario
Add fuzzing jobs for streaming frames to catch framing edge cases
Integrate contract tests into CI with a compatibility gate that can be toggled for daily runs
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Internal canary with infra team – enable bridge for two internal tenants (1 day)
Stage 2: Sandbox customers opt-in (week-long observation) – collect diff reports and session replays
Stage 3: Limited public opt-in (10 customers) with SLO monitoring and on-call readiness
Stage 4: Decide deprecation timeline for bridge once native runtime reaches parity or when customer migration completes
notes_for_release: Mark feature as beta in runtime-1.20 release notes. Include migration guide and example cURL snippets. Offer assisted migration for customers flagged high-risk.
customer_communication: Prepare template emails and customer-facing FAQ explaining opt-in compatibility mode, expected behaviors, and how to request support. Provide sample delta-report for each interested customer.
postmortem_triggers: More than 5 customer regressions in first 30 days
P99 latency increase > 200ms attributed to bridge
Data lossiness events classified as 'severe' in telemetry
